children: TRex Bio filed a final prospectus for its initial public offering, pricing 8,333,334 shares at $14.00 per share. The company has been approved to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker “TRXB,” with gross proceeds expected to be approximately $116.7 million before underwriting discounts and expenses. Underwriters have a 30‑day option to purchase up to 1,250,000 additional shares, and Eli Lilly has indicated interest in purchasing shares to hold up to 19.9% post‑offering.

TRex Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing immunoregulatory medicines that aim to restore immune balance and promote tissue repair by targeting regulatory T cells (Tregs) in diseased tissues. Built on its proprietary Deep Biology platform, the company identifies and validates targets that augment tissue Tregs, linking human tissue insights with translational strategies to guide drug design and development.

Its lead wholly owned candidate, TRB-061, is a selective TNFR2 agonist designed to expand and activate Tregs in inflamed tissues. TRB-061 is in a Phase 1b study in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, with topline data expected in mid‑2027, and potential expansion into alopecia areata. The second program, TRB-071, is a CD30 agonist antibody intended to both activate Tregs and modulate inflammatory signaling, with a Phase 1 trial planned for the first half of 2027. Beyond its wholly owned pipeline, TRex Bio has a collaboration with Eli Lilly that originated TRB-051, which Lilly is advancing, including plans for a Phase 2a study in lupus with cutaneous involvement.
: Atopic dermatitis impacts ~16 million U.S. adults and ~225 million people globally; IBD affects ~3 million Americans and is expected to exceed 10 million patients worldwide by 2032.
: Rising prevalence of immune-mediated diseases and continued biologics/small‑molecule adoption support sustained category growth.
: Early-stage clinical company focused on tissue regulatory T cell (Treg) biology with a platform designed to discover and develop immunoregulatory therapies.
: Existing AD and IBD treatments from large and specialty pharma (e.g., IL-4/13 inhibitors such as dupilumab; JAK inhibitors), and emerging Treg‑modulating approaches.
: Shift from broad immunosuppression toward targeted immunoregulation; increasing interest in Treg augmentation and tissue‑repair mechanisms.
: Headquarters and labs in South San Francisco, California
: United States-focused operations and clinical development
: Strategic collaboration with Eli Lilly; TRB-051 originated from TRex platform and is being advanced by Lilly
: Approximately 60 full-time employees as of August 31, 2026; cash runway projected into the second half of 2029 per use-of-proceeds plan
: Down from $39.1 million in 2024 to $0 in 2025 as collaboration revenue recognition concluded
: Net loss: $(34.8) million in 2025; $(29.3) million for the six months ended June 30, 2026
, Chief Executive Officer and Chair - Over 40 years in pharma leadership at Eli Lilly; led Lilly New Ventures and prior global regulatory submissions for Evista and Forteo.
, Chief Operating Officer - 25 years in strategy, corporate development, and legal; prior roles at Myovant, Roche/Genentech; leads business and corporate development.
, Chief Financial Officer - 25+ years in biotech finance; former CFO at Applied Molecular Transport; prior roles at Singulex, Novartis Vaccines & Diagnostics, and Genentech.
, Chief Medical Officer - 20+ years in immunology clinical development; previously at Biora and Genentech/Roche; former attending physician at Stanford University.
, Chief Scientific Officer - 25+ years in immunology and translational R&D led development of TRex’s Deep Biology platform; former Genentech R&D leader.
: J.P. Morgan; Evercore ISI; Cantor; Stifel; Wedbush PacGrow

: Approximately $103.5 million net to fund Phase 2 trials of TRB-061 in atopic dermatitis and alopecia areata through topline data, initiate and complete a Phase 1 trial of TRB-071 in healthy volunteers, and for working capital and general corporate purposes.
